title: docs(spec): a notify node's `recipients` names a written-out email address as an author constant, not an audience selector
body:
Fixes #25696

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: semantic
Ruling-ref: 6386629237

## What this changes

The `domain:spec` half of ruling B on #25647 (`6386629237`, batch #12 item 2, maintainer 「25635  25647  25675 同意」):

> 「**B** = 只关「表达式算出来的地址」：`notify` 收件人若由表达式（CEL 信封）求值得到一个不属于任何用户的邮箱地址，节点失败并给出定位提示指向 `{ emailField }`；求值得到某个用户的地址仍解析为该用户。元数据里**写死**的地址是作者常量，照常发出。」

Its spec workload: 「`domain:spec` 改描述文字，把「写死地址」写成作者常量，并从受众选择器列表里去掉笼统的「an email address」。」

Text only, all in `packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts`. No key, shape, default, enum or accepted value moves; everything that parsed still parses.

- **The `recipients` docblock** (the `NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema` JSDoc):
  - "an email address" is gone from the audience-selector list, which now reads "(such as `team:ID`)".
  - A string address the author writes out is named an **author constant**, sent as written: to the user who holds it, or else, on the `email` channel, to the address itself.
  - A paragraph states what the runtime half (#25721, `d1e329e96d`, `screenComputedAddresses` in service-automation's notify node) makes. In a node whose `channels` include `email`, a computed recipient that reads as an address, bare or as `user:ADDRESS`, must be a user's. One a user holds resolves to that user. One that no user holds, or one that cannot be looked up, fails the node, pointing to `{ emailField }`.
  - A node that does not name `email` mails nobody, and its computed recipients reach the messaging resolver unscreened, as before. That channel scope is confirmed (ruling record 6393736930 on #25647).
  - A second paragraph states the email-field delivery the same change makes: the address is read from the stored trigger row and must be one plain ASCII mailbox. One address receives at most 5 sends per hour, best-effort.
- **The field `.describe()`** (what the reference docs and the JSON Schema read) and **the union's `.meta()` description** say the same.
  - The `.describe()` sentence "Delivery to an email-field recipient is not live yet: until the messaging service resolves the form, a run that reaches the node fails there" is replaced with what the runtime does.
- **`NOTIFY_RECIPIENTS_RULE`**, the sentence a refused `recipients` value leads with, now lists "an email address written out, an author constant sent as written" beside a user id and an audience selector. A refused author is told every string spelling. Its opening, "`recipients` is who the notification goes to", is unchanged (pinned by `io-node-config.test.ts`).
- **The email-field section note** no longer calls `{ emailField }` "the one recipient form that is an email ADDRESS". It is the form for an address the record supplies, and it is delivered since `d1e329e96d`. An address written out by the author is the other way to one.
- Regenerated `content/docs/references/automation/io-node-config.mdx` with `gen:docs`, and added the changeset `.changeset/25696-notify-recipients-describe.md` (`@objectstack/spec`: `minor`, the level `Metadata-protocol: semantic` takes).

## The refusal is made: the runtime half landed

When this PR opened, the computed-address refusal was worded as planned, because the runtime half was still open (triage `6387591836`). PR #25721 (`d1e329e96d`) has since landed the runtime half for both #25571 and #25647, and this branch merged it (`f6c07d3953`). The text now states what is made, read from the merged `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts`:

- `resolveRecipients` marks each recipient that an envelope computed and that reads as an address (`mailedAddressOf`: bare, or the remainder after `user:`).
- `screenComputedAddresses` runs only when `toStringList(cfg.channels).includes('email')`.
- `resolveEmailFieldAddress` reads the stored row and requires `isOneAddress`.
- `admitEmailFieldSend` caps sends at `EMAIL_FIELD_SENDS_PER_WINDOW` (5) per `EMAIL_FIELD_SEND_WINDOW_SECONDS` (3600), and admits on a counter fault.
- A written-out address never reaches the screen.

## What each claim in the new text rests on

- *A written-out address reaches the user who holds it, or else, on the `email` channel, the address itself:* `RecipientResolver.resolveOne` → `resolveEmail` (a `sys_user` lookup by `email`, verbatim on a miss), then `email-channel.ts`'s `EMAIL_SHAPE(recipient)` branch. `screenComputedAddresses` never sees a written-out value.
- *Computed address, email node:* `screenComputedAddresses`, quoted above.
- *Computed address, non-email node:* the `mails` gate in `registerNotifyNode` passes `audience.value.recipients` through unscreened.
- *Email-field delivery:* `resolveEmailFieldAddress`, `isOneAddress` and `admitEmailFieldSend`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Hand-written docs:** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` now carries #25721's paragraphs on the email-field form and the computed-address rule (from `:359`). They match the runtime and this text, so I changed nothing there. `:340` still lists a user id and `team:ID` and never calls a bare address a selector, so it is not false. The runtime's own texts and the migration entry `18.flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused.ts:90` are not false either.
- **Pending changeset made false by #25721, not by this PR:** the last paragraph of `.changeset/25610-notify-email-field-recipient.md` says delivery "lands separately; until it does, a run that reaches such a node fails at the node". That has been false since #25721 (`d1e329e96d`). This PR does not correct it: the release-note gate (#17712, `check-empty-changeset`) holds a correction of another PR's pending changeset red until a person confirms it, so the seat has filed it for the maintainer as a separate decision, #25754.
- **Downstream producers, measured (anonymous reads):**
  - objectui `7981384`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowRecipientsField.tsx:15`: the "Email address" row stores an author constant, unaffected.
  - The "Record field" row (`:12`) stores `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.FIELD' }`. Over an `email`-typed field on an `email` node, that is now refused unless a user holds the address. Routing such fields to `{ emailField }` belongs to the runtime lane.
  - hotcrm `8a14b56`: no written-out recipient address.
  - `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts`: `exec@example.com` (`:1435`) and `admin@objectos.ai` ×4 (`:430`, `:1454`, `:1567`, `:1730`) are author constants. No showcase `notify` node names the `email` channel.
